name: Ward Nine: The Involuntary Substrate Trials
description: Assembled over six years by investigative documentarian Oluwafunmilayo Brandt-Szeto, this film uses smuggled medical records, survivor testimony recorded on analog equipment, and two whistleblower depositions to document HelixCorp's forced neural substrate migration experiments conducted on non-consenting the Gray Zone residents in Ward Nine between 2189 and 2198. The film exists only on physical media — crystalline data chips circulated through dead drops — because streaming any segment triggers automated HelixCorp surveillance flags. Brandt-Szeto disappeared four months after the first copies began circulating; her body was recovered from Lake Michigan in 2205, ruled accidental.
cultural_impact: The film's existence — even as rumor — created the phrase 'Ward Nine' as the Gray Zone slang for any medical intervention you didn't choose and can't refuse.
story_hooks: A runner is hired to transport a chip they're told contains music; when their BCI accidentally interfaces with it during a close call, they see thirty seconds of Ward Nine footage.
One of the surviving Ward Nine test subjects, now living under a false substrate identity, recognizes themselves in a still image from the film that's been posted to an underground mesh node.
A HelixCorp internal security team is hunting the last known copy of the original master file, which they believe contains the name of a current Spire executive.
